chunks: From him, from one of our companions, from Al-Asamm, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat the endive, for there is no morning but that a drop from Paradise descends upon it. So when you eat it, do not shake it off.'
He said: And Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) forbade us from shaking it off whenever we ate it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءَ: Endive, a type of leafy green vegetable

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of eating endive according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* underscores the medicinal and spiritual virtues of endive (*hindaba*), linking its daily consumption to divine sustenance through the metaphor of a 'drop from Paradise.' The instruction not to shake off the dew emphasizes the appreciation of natural blessings and reflects the practical health wisdom preserved in Shia hadith literature regarding dietary habits.

en.hubeali: From him, from one of our companions, from Al Samma, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat the endive, for there is none from the mornings except that there descends upon it a drop from the Paradise. So when you eat it, so do not shake it off’.
He (the narrator) said: ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> forbade us<sup>asws</sup> from shaking it whenever we<sup>asws</sup> ate it’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain persons of our people from al-Asamm from Shu’ayb from abu Basir who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘You should eat endives. Every morning one drop descends on it from paradise and when you eat it do not shake it off.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, prohibited us from shaking off when we ate endives.’”
